observations.explanation: The paper reports 12.47% resolved (286/2,294) on the full SWE-bench test set (PDF pp. 5–6).

The Lite-split ablations compare interface variants: editing without linting scores 15.0% versus 18.0%, and the search ablations also show performance differences (PDF pp. 6–7). These provide evidence that interface choices affect performance.

The authors say the final ACI design was reached through qualitative analysis on a small set of hand-picked easier development examples (PDF p. 5). The claim appropriately frames generalization as unresolved rather than as a demonstrated defect.

The evaluation is limited to two LMs and the stated benchmark setup (PDF p. 5); although the paper reports results with Claude 3 Opus as well, broader transfer is not established. The statement that this assessment does not include independent reproduction is also qualified as a scope statement, not a claim about the paper’s results.
